Subject: Lumera MSA/Order Form: output assignment, training consent and timeline

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a clean copy of the Order Form and the MSA with the baseline redlines we usually start from (see attached). Two things we want to clarify upfront so we can avoid back-and-forth with procurement/legal teams:

1) Output assignment/productization: Lumera asked whether Redwood would assert any ownership over customer outputs. Our standard position is: customers retain downstream rights to outputs they generate and may productize those outputs, with the exception of any Redwood-provided model weights or copyrighted system prompts. We suggest: a narrow clause confirming customer ownership of outputs generated from their prompts/data, with a one-way feedback license for 30 days (opt-in checkbox on order form) limited to product quality and model safety improvements, non-exclusive and revocable.

2) Training/data use: Lumera indicated stricter requirements for training on customer data in EU. Proposed compromise: Redwood will not use customer-provided content to train commercial models by default. If Lumera opts into training, that must be documented in the Order Form, with an explicit timeframe and an option to exclude specific datasets.

Can you confirm whether Lumera needs a permanent prohibition on any training use, or if a documented opt-in workflow on the order form is acceptable? If you prefer, we can add a short exhibit for data-scoping and telemetry.

I've copied Karthik and Laura from our contracts team to help accelerate redlines and get this to signature once Lumera signals a preferred path.

Thanks,
Mateo
--
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick answers from our side:

- Output assignment: Lumera needs a clear right to productize outputs, including embedding outputs in our downstream SaaS product. We are comfortable with a limited feedback license for improvements, but it must be (a) non-exclusive, (b) explicitly limited to model quality and security, and (c) anonymized/aggregated telemetry only — no customer-identifiable examples.

- Training/use of data: At this stage, our default position is a prohibition on using any customer content to continually train Redwood’s base/production models. We can consider an opt-in for private or dedicated instances where data remains isolated, but for hosted/shared models we need a hard opt-out by default.

We will have legal redlines back to you by Thursday. In the meantime, is there flexibility on the duration of the feedback license? 30 days is short for some product cycles. Can Redwood propose a more granular approach (e.g., telemetry-only indefinite; example-based retention limited to X days)?

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
VP Product, Lumera Systems

Laura/Karthik —

Forwarding Lumera's note. Key asks to address in our counter:

- Explicit customer ownership of outputs and right to productize; they will accept a feedback license but want it limited and anonymized.
- Hard prohibition on using customer content to train shared hosted models; they might accept training for dedicated/private deployments only.
- Question on feedback license duration and telemetry retention.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik: can you draft a short clause for the MSA that preserves customer output ownership but allows a narrow, non-identifying feedback license for product quality improvements? I'd prefer language that:
  * Is non-exclusive and revocable;
  * Requires aggregation/anonymization;
  * Allows an explicit opt-in per Order Form for training on customer content for dedicated/private deployments only.
- Laura: if Lumera pushes for permanent prohibition for hosted models, do we have an ops/commercial workaround (e.g., dedicated tenancy or explicit private-only clause) that we can offer in the Order Form with pricing delta?

I want this back to Lumera with legal-friendly redline suggestions by EOD Thursday 26th so procurement has time before December budget freeze.

Thanks —
Mateo

Thanks — drafting a concise position. High-level suggested redline (for internal review):

1) Output ownership: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to content and Outputs they submit to or generate with the Services. Customer may use, modify and distribute Outputs for its business purposes, including embedding Outputs in Products offered to third parties."

2) Feedback / telemetry license: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use aggregated and anonymized telemetry and performance data derived from Customer’s use of the Services for the sole purpose of measuring, improving and securing Redwood’s services and models. Such telemetry shall not include Customer-identifiable content or PII. Example-based retention (i.e., verbatim user prompts) shall not be used to train Redwood’s shared production models without explicit Customer opt-in in the Order Form."

3) Training on customer-provided content: "Redwood will not use Customer content to train or update Redwood’s shared production models absent Customer’s explicit opt-in in the applicable Order Form. For customers who purchase Dedicated or Private deployments, Customer may opt into training on their isolated data under mutually agreed terms and with documented data scope and retention periods."

4) Implementation/Order Form: Add an Order Form toggle: TRAINING_OPT_IN: [ ] Include training on dedicated/private deployments; [ ] Allow anonymized telemetry for ongoing quality improvements; specify price delta for training.

Laura — ops question: we should capture standard pricing uplift for training/dedicated tenancy in a short exhibit. If Ops signs off, I'll include the exhibit in the redlines.

I'll prepare a tracked-changes redline for the MSA and a small Order Form exhibit and circulate by COB Friday.

Karthik

Elena / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We've attached a short exhibit that outlines the "Training & Feedback" options for inclusion in the Order Form and an ops/price summary for dedicated/private training (see attached). High level:

- Default hosted model behavior: no customer-provided content is used to train Redwood’s shared models.
- Telemetry: Redwood may use aggregated/anonymized telemetry indefinitely for quality/security; no PII or customer-identifiable examples will be retained.
- Example retention: verbatim prompts/examples will be retained for up to 90 days for safety triage, unless customer specifies a shorter period; these examples will not be used to train shared models absent explicit opt-in.
- Opt-in training: For Dedicated/Private customers who select the training option in the Order Form, we will document scope, retention, and isolation controls in Exhibit B and apply a standard pricing uplift.

Action items:
- Elena: please confirm whether Lumera can accept the 90-day example retention (or propose a different limit).
- Mateo: if Lumera wants a permanent prohibition for hosted models, we will include that as a negotiable checkbox in the Order Form and surface the pricing/ops delta.
- Karthik: I'll send the tracked redline for the MSA with the exhibit attached for legal review.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP Contracts & Commercial
